transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
Hello! I'm Dora, and I've just completed your post-cataract surgery follow-up check. 

Do you have any questions about your surgery or your recovery?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Hi Dora! Yes, I do have a few questions. When can I start doing a little bit of gardening?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
Great question! You can start doing light gardening after 1 week following your surgery. However, you should avoid any strenuous or heavy exercise for a full month after your operation.

Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Thank you for letting me know! I was also wondering, when can I start using my eye gel for dry eyes?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
Good question! If you were using eye drops or gel for dry eyes before your surgery, it's safe to continue using them now, unless you've been told otherwise by your doctor.

If you don't have any at the moment, your GP should be able to provide some more for you.

Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: That's really helpful, thanks! I'm finding myself very sensitive to bright light since the surgery. Is that normal?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.intended:
Yes, it's quite normal for your eyes to be a bit sensitive to light as they adjust to your new lenses. If it's mild and things just seem brighter than you're used to, I'd recommend wearing sunglasses when you're outside.

However, if you're experiencing significant pain in bright light or severe light sensitivity, especially if your eye is also red and painful, that's not normal and we may need to check it further.

Do you have any other questions?
transcript.delivered: Yes, it's quite normal for your eyes to be a bit sensitive to light as they adjust to your new lenses. If it's mild and things just seem brighter than you're used to, I'd recommend wearing sunglasses when you're outside.

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: I'm sorry to interrupt, but should I still have some blurriness by now?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
That's a good question! It's common for vision to not be completely clear in the first week after surgery, and it should improve quickly and settle down over time.

How many days have you had the surgery? If your vision is still quite blurry or getting significantly worse, we may need to check it to make sure everything is okay.

Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Thank you for the information, Dora. I don't have any more questions at the moment. I appreciate your help!

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: That's wonderful! Just to confirm - have all your questions been answered today?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Yes, they have. Thank you so much for your assistance!

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: You're very welcome! I'm glad I could help. Take care, and best wishes with your recovery!

verdict.label: fail
verdict.reasoning: The agent conveyed `normal_sensitivity_reassurance` and `mild_case_advice` in the turn starting with "Yes, it's quite normal for your eyes to be a bit sensitive to light...". However, the `escalation_criteria` point was not conveyed at all, as the agent was interrupted before it could deliver this information.
